```{r}
data <- readRDS(params$data_file)
p <- data
overview <- p$dataset_overview
manifest <- p$summary_manifest
status <- as.character(manifest$status[[1L]])

escape_html <- function(x) {
  x <- ifelse(is.na(x), "", as.character(x))
  x <- gsub("&", "&amp;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("<", "&lt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub(">", "&gt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  gsub('"', "&quot;", x, fixed = TRUE)
}
fmt <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x) | !nzchar(as.character(x)), "-", as.character(x))
table_html <- function(x) {
  if (nrow(x) == 0L) return("No rows to display.")
  knitr::kable(x, format = "html", escape = TRUE)
}
section_rows <- function(...) {
  rows <- list(...)
  ids <- unique(unlist(lapply(rows, function(x) if (nrow(x)) as.character(x$section_id) else character())))
  ids[!is.na(ids) & nzchar(ids)]
}
wrap_label <- function(x, width = 36L) {
  vapply(x, function(value) paste(strwrap(as.character(value), width = width), collapse = "\n"), character(1))
}
```

::: {.callout-note}
**`r params$report_title`**

This report describes de-identified Initial Epidemiological Interview data for
controlled analytical use. It does not contain the private re-identification
crosswalk and is not automatically suitable for unrestricted public release.
:::

```{r, results='asis'}
if (identical(status, "review")) {
  cat("::: {.callout-warning}\n**Analytical status: REVIEW**\n\nReview findings remain in the summary products; interpret this report accordingly.\n:::\n")
} else {
  cat("::: {.callout-note}\n**Analytical status: PASSED**\n\nThe summary products passed the configured analytical gates.\n:::\n")
}
```

## Dataset overview

The values below are supplied by `summarize_epi()` in `dataset_overview.csv`.

```{r, results='asis'}
overview_table <- data.frame(
  Measure = c("Cases", "Counties represented", "Interview date range",
              "Validation: valid cases", "Validation: review cases",
              "Validation: error cases", "Repeated-table records"),
  Value = c(
    overview$n_cases[[1L]], overview$n_counties[[1L]],
    paste(fmt(overview$first_interview_date[[1L]]), "to", fmt(overview$last_interview_date[[1L]])),
    overview$n_validation_valid[[1L]], overview$n_validation_review[[1L]],
    overview$n_validation_error[[1L]], overview$n_repeated_records[[1L]]
  )
)
cat(table_html(overview_table))
```

## Validation status

```{r, results='asis'}
validation <- p$validation_status_summary
validation$validation_status <- factor(validation$validation_status,
  levels = c("valid", "review", "error"))
print(ggplot2::ggplot(validation, ggplot2::aes_string(
  x = "validation_status", y = "n_cases", fill = "validation_status"
)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Validation status", y = "Cases") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c(valid = "#3b7d5a", review = "#9a6b20", error = "#a94a4a"),
    drop = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank()))
cat("\n\n", table_html(validation), sep = "")
```

## Questionnaire summaries by section

Categorical percentages and counts in this section are displayed directly from
the scalar and multiselect summary products. Percentages use the denominator
specified in each product.

```{r, results='asis'}
scalar <- p$scalar_frequencies
multi <- p$multiselect_frequencies
repeated_categorical <- p$repeated_categorical_frequencies
sections <- section_rows(scalar, multi, repeated_categorical)
for (section_id in sections) {
  section_name <- c(
    as.character(scalar$section_name[scalar$section_id == section_id]),
    as.character(multi$section_name[multi$section_id == section_id]),
    as.character(repeated_categorical$section_name[repeated_categorical$section_id == section_id])
  )
  section_name <- section_name[!is.na(section_name) & nzchar(section_name)][1L]
  cat("### Section ", escape_html(section_id),
      if (!is.na(section_name)) paste0(": ", escape_html(section_name)) else "", "\n\n", sep = "")
  section_scalar <- scalar[scalar$section_id == section_id, , drop = FALSE]
  for (question_id in unique(as.character(section_scalar$question_id))) {
    current <- section_scalar[section_scalar$question_id == question_id, , drop = FALSE]
    question_text <- current$question_text[[1L]]
    cat("#### ", escape_html(question_id), ": ", escape_html(question_text), "\n\n", sep = "")
    current$response_label <- fmt(current$response_label)
    if (all(as.numeric(current$n_answered) == 0)) {
      cat("No responses recorded. Missing: ", current$n_missing[[1L]],
          " of ", current$n_cases_total[[1L]], " cases.\n\n", sep = "")
      next
    }
    if (nrow(current) <= 8L) {
      response_levels <- current$response_label[order(current$response_order,
        seq_len(nrow(current)), na.last = TRUE)]
      current$response_label <- factor(current$response_label,
        levels = unique(response_levels))
      print(ggplot2::ggplot(current, ggplot2::aes_string(
        x = "percent_of_answered", y = "response_label"
      )) +
        ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "#2c6e8f") +
        ggplot2::labs(x = "Percent of answered cases", y = NULL) +
        ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(labels = wrap_label) +
        ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
        ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank()))
    } else {
      display <- current[c("response_label", "n_response", "percent_of_answered", "n_answered", "n_missing", "n_cases_total")]
      names(display) <- c("Response", "Responses", "Percent of answered", "Answered", "Missing", "Cases")
      cat(table_html(display), "\n\n", sep = "")
    }
    cat("<p class='epi-caption'>Response categories: ",
        paste(vapply(as.character(current$response_label), escape_html, character(1)),
          collapse = ", "), ".</p>\n", sep = "")
    cat("<p class='epi-caption'>Answered: ", current$n_answered[[1L]], " of ",
        current$n_cases_total[[1L]], " cases; missing: ", current$n_missing[[1L]],
        ". Zero-count codebook categories are retained.</p>\n", sep = "")
  }
  section_multi <- multi[multi$section_id == section_id, , drop = FALSE]
  for (question_id in unique(as.character(section_multi$question_id))) {
    current <- section_multi[section_multi$question_id == question_id, , drop = FALSE]
    cat("#### ", escape_html(question_id), ": ", escape_html(current$question_text[[1L]]), "\n\n", sep = "")
    current$item_label <- fmt(current$item_label)
    current$item_label <- factor(current$item_label, levels = rev(current$item_label))
    print(ggplot2::ggplot(current, ggplot2::aes_string(
      x = "percent_of_all_cases", y = "item_label"
    )) +
      ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "#6b8e9e") +
      ggplot2::labs(x = "Percent of all cases", y = "Selected item") +
      ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(labels = wrap_label) +
      ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
      ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank()))
    cat("<p class='epi-caption'>Cases with any selection: ",
        current$n_cases_with_any_selection[[1L]],
        ". Percentages within a multiselect question need not sum to 100%.</p>\n", sep = "")
  }
}
```

## Repeated-table overview

The repeated-table products retain all registered tables, including tables with
zero records. Categorical percentages below use records with a nonmissing
response, not cases.

```{r, results='asis'}
tables <- p$repeated_table_summaries
display <- tables[c("table_name", "n_cases_with_records", "n_records_total",
                    "median_records_per_case", "max_records_per_case")]
names(display) <- c("Table", "Cases with records", "Total records",
                    "Median records per case", "Maximum records per case")
cat(table_html(display), "\n\n", sep = "")
if (nrow(repeated_categorical) > 0L) {
  repeated_display <- repeated_categorical[c(
    "table_name", "column_name", "response_label", "n_records_total",
    "n_nonmissing", "n_value", "percent_of_nonmissing")]
  names(repeated_display) <- c("Table", "Column", "Response", "Records",
    "Nonmissing records", "Value count", "Percent of nonmissing records")
  cat(table_html(repeated_display))
}
```

## Numeric summaries

These are descriptive summaries supplied by `numeric_summaries.csv`. The
report does not reconstruct distributions from aggregate statistics.

```{r, results='asis'}
numeric <- p$numeric_summaries
numeric_display <- numeric[c("section_id", "question_id", "canonical_name", "units",
  "n_parsed", "n_unparsed", "n_missing", "mean", "sd", "median", "q25", "q75", "min", "max")]
cat(table_html(numeric_display), "\n\n", sep = "")
plot_data <- numeric[!is.na(numeric$median), , drop = FALSE]
if (nrow(plot_data) > 0L) {
  plot_data$label <- ifelse(is.na(plot_data$units) | !nzchar(plot_data$units),
    plot_data$canonical_name, paste0(plot_data$canonical_name, " (", plot_data$units, ")"))
  print(ggplot2::ggplot(plot_data, ggplot2::aes_string(x = "label", y = "median")) +
    ggplot2::geom_linerange(ggplot2::aes_string(ymin = "min", ymax = "max"), colour = "#9aaab2", linewidth = 1) +
    ggplot2::geom_errorbar(ggplot2::aes_string(ymin = "q25", ymax = "q75"), width = .2, colour = "#2c6e8f", linewidth = 2) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.5, colour = "#24313a") +
    ggplot2::coord_flip() + ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Value") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank()))
}
```

## Date summaries

Date ranges and parsing counts are displayed directly from `date_summaries.csv`.

```{r, results='asis'}
dates <- p$date_summaries[c("section_id", "question_id", "canonical_name",
  "n_parsed", "n_unparsed", "n_missing", "min_date", "median_date", "max_date")]
cat(table_html(dates))
```

## Notes on denominators and missingness

Categorical summaries distinguish answered cases from missing cases. Explicit
answered categories such as `Not applicable` remain response categories. Scalar
categorical percentages use `percent_of_answered`; multiselect percentages show
their denominator in the axis and caption; repeated categorical percentages use
records with a nonmissing response.
